Fixes #4151.

This pull request removes the `--private` and `--public` flags from `gh repo list`:

```bash
$  ./bin/gh repo list --public          
unknown flag: --public

Usage:  gh repo list [<owner>] [flags]

Flags:
      --archived            Show only archived rep
...
```

Instead, it used the `--visibility` flag, which can be `public`, `private`, or `internal`.

I can change the approach to introduce an `--internal` flag to maintain backward compatibility. I didn't go with that route because:

- [This](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4151#issuecomment-1010130213) comments.
- Even if we go with that route, to maintain consistency, `--private` would only show private repos which would alter the behavior for users who saw internal repositories with `--private`. 

Thanks in advance.

issue_context.title: Repo list: repositories with "internal" visibility are displayed as "private"
issue_context.body:
We use GraphQL to list repositories, and `Repository.isPrivate` for internal repositories is true. However, instead of "private" we should be displaying "internal". This information is available through the REST API for repositories, but I cannot find whether it's exposed in the GraphQL API.

Ref. https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/2953
Loosely related: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2106
comments:
I've discovered the `Repository.visibility` GraphQL field which seems to be present from at least GHE 2.20, which means it would be safe for us to use unconditionally in our codebase. We should switch from `isPrivate` to looking at `visibility` when rendering repository information to correctly discern between "private" and "internal" repositories.

Furthermore, `gh repo list --private` should not include "internal" repositories, as there should be a new flag to list internal ones, probably `--internal` (or `--visibility=internal` if we would want to consolidate all visibility flags into one). This might be tricky, since neither the `repositories` GraphQL connection nor the Search API that we use in some cases support filtering by "internal" visibility. Until the API allows filtering, we could request all "private" repositories (which currently includes "internal" ones) and do filtering client-side.

review_comments: Removing these flags breaks backwards compatibility. I would suggest leaving them in and having them be the equivalent of passing `--visibility private/public`.

I agree we should not remove these, which is why I think it would actually be less confusing to our users to just add a `--internal` flag instead of a more generic `--visibility` flag. Not a super strong opinion on this one but thought I would chime in.
